stories.headline: US envoys meet Putin in Moscow as Russia orders three-day pause in Kyiv strikes
stories.body:
US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Saturday.

Kirill Dmitriev, who is Putin's investment envoy, received the two American envoys in the Russian capital. US President Donald Trump said on Friday that Witkoff and Kushner were bringing a proposal to end the war. Russian state media reported that the meeting between Putin and the envoys at the Kremlin lasted three hours. At the start of the meeting, Putin said it is convenient for Russia to work with Witkoff and Kushner. But Putin also told the envoys that the current situation is not so easy.

During the meeting, Witkoff thanked Putin for agreeing with Ukraine to stop strikes on each other's capital cities for three days. Putin ordered a three-day halt to strikes on Kyiv because of the visit by the US envoys. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said Putin gave the order to stop strikes starting from midnight Saturday. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine is ready to refrain from strikes on Moscow through the end of Saturday, as well as on Sunday and Monday. Witkoff and Kushner are scheduled to travel to Kyiv on Sunday for diplomatic engagements. CIA Director John Ratcliffe made a rare visit to Moscow a little over a week before Witkoff and Kushner arrived.

Putin said in televised remarks that Russia has not agreed to a ceasefire in areas of Ukraine outside of Kyiv. Ground troops in Ukraine remain locked along a 775-mile frontline. Zelensky said Russia fired demonstrative strikes on airports in Kyiv and Boryspil overnight before his planned meeting with the envoys. On Friday, a Russian drone hit the headquarters of the Security Service of Ukraine. Russian strikes killed at least seven people across Ukraine on Saturday, including two in the Bucha district outside Kyiv. Zelensky said an overnight Russian strike on a civilian building in the Dnipro region killed four people and injured five others. Oleksandr Hanzha, head of the local military administration, said an overnight Russian strike at a factory in the Dnipropetrovsk region killed five people and wounded five others.

stories.headline: US military disables three Iranian oil tankers following attacks on warships
stories.body:
US Central Command said its forces permanently disabled two Iran-linked oil tankers and completely destroyed a third in the Gulf of Oman. US Central Command said the strikes retaliated after Tehran targeted a US aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer. US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth posted on social media that if Iran shoots at US ships, the US will destroy and sink their oil tankers. US Central Command commander Admiral Brad Cooper said the US military would destroy Iran's oil fleet if necessary to defend American forces.

US Central Command identified the disabled tankers as M/T Downy, struck off Kharg Island, and M/T Stark 1, struck near Jask. Kharg Island hosts Iran's main oil export terminal, handling about 90% of the country's crude oil exports via pipes from the mainland. US Central Command identified the destroyed third tanker as M/T Kylo, which is also known as Noxen.

The US resumed attacks after striking two rocket launchers to stop Iran from laying naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian state media reported that Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps retaliated against six ships. These included three oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and three US-affiliated vessels.

US Vice President JD Vance said he was extremely sceptical about Iranian claims that US strikes killed four people at a wedding in Sirik. A preliminary US military inquiry found a February 28 strike on a school compound in Minab killed at least 156 people. The inquiry found outdated coordinates had identified the school as part of a naval base. The average price for a gallon of diesel in the US reached $5.85, up from $3.71 a year prior.

stories.headline: Rescuers pull survivors from wreckage days after flood disaster in Nepal and China
stories.body:
Rescue teams pulled survivors from flood wreckage in Nepal and China days after a massive disaster. Rescuers pulled Chandika Kumari Shrestha, who is 64 years old, semi-conscious from a buried house in Betrawati 10 days after floods hit Nepal. Local officials in Betrawati said only five out of about 300 houses remained standing after the flood. A joint team of Nepal army personnel and South Korean experts rescued Chinese worker Luhaitao from a tunnel. Luhaitao was rescued 225 metres inside a tunnel at the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project and flown to a military hospital. The Upper Trishuli-1 project is valued at about $647m.

A collapse of ice, rock, and mud swept through a Himalayan valley in Nepal. Nepal's national disaster authority reported that the flood killed at least 1,331 people. Nepal's disaster management agency reported that at least 1,375 people died. The disaster left about 5,000 people missing, including 589 foreign nationals. Officials in Tibet recorded 31 deaths and 531 people missing across the border.

About 900 workers remain unaccounted for at hydropower construction sites in Nepal, with roughly 500 believed trapped inside tunnels. The floods severely damaged 12 hydropower plants in the Trishuli River basin and knocked out over 10% of Nepal's power capacity. Nearly 100% of Nepal's electricity comes from hydropower.

stories.headline: UN adopts resolution approving world map that shows true size of countries
stories.body:
The United Nations voted on Friday to support moving away from the 16th-century Mercator map toward a map showing true country sizes. The UN General Assembly adopted the Correct the Map resolution to fix discrepancies in the Mercator map projection. Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator created the Mercator map in 1569 to aid European sailors in ocean navigation. The African continent is about 14 times larger than Greenland, despite looking similar in size on the Mercator map.

Togo introduced the resolution at the UN on behalf of 54 African member states, supported by the African Union. Togo's Foreign Minister Robert Dussey said a fair map does not change geography, but changes how the world is seen. A team of cartographers created the Equal Earth projection in 2018, and African Union members adopted it in February.

The UN resolution passed with 164 countries voting in favour, one voting against, and six abstaining. India voted in favour of the resolution, while the United States was the only country to vote against it. US representative Yaryna Ferencevych said resolutions like Correct the Map cause the UN to lose credibility. The US delegation claimed the resolution was part of a larger radical political project. Ukraine abstained over concerns about how some Equal Earth maps depict Ukrainian territories occupied by Russia.

stories.headline: PM Modi addresses SRCC centenary, defends GDP growth and warns Pakistan
stories.body:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the centenary celebrations at Shri Ram College of Commerce in Delhi on Saturday evening. Modi previously spoke at the college in February 2013 while serving as Chief Minister of Gujarat. Modi recalled his 2013 glass analogy, saying he sees the glass as full, with half water and half air. Modi is serving his third consecutive term as Prime Minister and completes 25 years as head of government next month.

Modi cited India's first-quarter GDP growth rate of 7.8 per cent as evidence of economic strength. Modi described critics of the GDP growth numbers as grumpy uncles who focus only on negativity. Modi said those who placed India among the fragile five economies cannot digest India's 7.8 per cent growth.

Former senior Finance Ministry official Subhash Chandra Garg claimed the 7.8 per cent growth rate was overstated due to base revisions. Garg said nominal GDP growth would be 2.6 per cent if the previous year's base was not revised down. Former RBI Governor Raghuram Rajan asked why strong growth has not led to higher private investment and job creation. India's Ministry of Statistics held a press briefing to defend the revised GDP methodology implemented in February.

Congress leader Kanhaiya Kumar called Modi's address a public relations campaign before student elections. Kumar said Modi focused on 2013 and 2047 while failing to address student or public issues. Congress MP Pawan Khera criticized Modi's speech on social media, writing that even onions would burst into tears.

Modi criticized the Congress party's student outreach campaign, called Chhatron Ki Goonj, describing it as an echo of lies. The campaign focuses on student issues including exam paper leaks, rising education costs, and unemployment. Modi said if Pakistan indulges in misadventure, Indian armed forces enter their territory and strike. Modi said his Independence Day reference to urban Naxals exposed political opponents like a homeopathic dose.

stories.headline: Indian government advances Census enumeration in four poll-bound states
stories.body:
The Indian government advanced the population enumeration phase of Census 2027 in four states. The enumeration in Uttar Pradesh, Goa, Punjab, and non-snow-bound Uttarakhand will run from December 1, 2026, to January 4, 2027. The reference date for the advanced Census enumeration in these four states is set for January 5, 2027. A revisional round for Census enumeration in these four states will take place from January 5 to January 9, 2027. A 15-day self-enumeration window for Census 2027 will open in the four states from November 16 to November 30, 2026.

Assembly elections are scheduled to take place in Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Goa, and Manipur in February-March 2027. Government officials said dates were advanced to prevent staffing conflicts between census duties and elections.

The Census phase in Manipur was deferred following local demands to conduct the National Register of Citizens exercise first. The Ministry of Home Affairs deferred the Manipur census on August 31 amid ongoing state violence.

Census 2027 will be India's first digital census and will collect caste data for the first time since 1931. The national population census was originally scheduled for 2021 but was delayed due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
